## Independent Georgia Register Reconciliation (State-Register Track)
- **Statutory rule (`GAC 110-37-2` & DCA HPD Fact Sheet):** National Register listings enter the Georgia Register automatically; Georgia Register approvals enter only state-level recognition first and require separate NPS submission (and do not list federally if a majority of private owners object). DCA confirms no single downloadable spreadsheet of pre-2023 state-only Georgia Register properties exists outside GNAHRGIS (`gnahrgis.org`).
- **2023–2026 Georgia National Register Review Board Reconciliation (all 34 approved resources + 6 pending/DOE 2026 items checked against NPS bulk file & 2026 Weekly Lists through `2026-11-13`):**
  1. **Brooks Historic District** (Brooks, Fayette County — approved Oct. 24, 2025; DCA press release Dec. 2, 2025): **State-only Georgia Register approval with NO federal NRHP listing.** Already filed as a real lead in Wave 2 (`ID BROOKS`; cross-referenced here so it is never dropped).
  2. **33 of 34 (May 2023 – Oct. 2025) Georgia Register approvals now hold federal NRHP listings:** including `New Ford Baptist Church & Cemetery` (`100012159`, listed Jul. 8, 2026), `R. M. Moore Elementary School` (`100012712`, approved as Waleska Elementary, listed Aug. 3, 2026), `Euharlee Elementary School` (`100012652`, listed Feb. 25, 2026), `First Federal Savings & Loan HQ` (`100012880`, listed Apr. 3, 2026), and `Milton Avenue School` (`100012513`, listed Nov. 12, 2026).

## Post-closeout thematic correction — Appling County (added Nov. 21, 2026, ~3:32 AM PT)

This correction does **not** reopen Georgia's completed federal/state register control. It adds six non-register thematic grounds missed by the mechanical closure pass. All six were collision-checked against the live 701-entry catalog, HT-US-INDEX, Southeast first sweep, haunted sweep, every Georgia Finder file, and the shared dossier lane; none was held elsewhere.

| Place | Town, County | Anchor | Family | Visitation tier & evidence signal | Source trail | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Holmesville first county-seat and courthouse/jail ground (1828–1873) | Former Holmesville, Appling County | **NONE** — the first courthouse burned in the 1850s, its successor was sold after the county seat moved, and no surviving public site or precise lawful viewpoint was verified | Prisons/Jails & Courts / County government | **Tier 4** — NO SIGNAL | https://dlg.usg.edu/record/dlg_gacoch_appling-county-courthouse · https://www.georgiahistory.com/ghmi_marker_updated/appling-county/ · https://dlg.usg.edu/record/dlg_ggpd_s-ga-ba400-pc7-bs1-bs78-b1900-h1976 | NO-ANCHOR; the Baxley marker that tells the county-seat sequence is currently out of place for damage or maintenance and is not a substitute anchor |
| Camp Alabax / CCC Camp P-62 and Veal's Still Site | Rural ground northeast of Baxley, Appling County | **NONE** — contemporary records place the forestry camp about five miles northeast of Baxley and the county plan names a Veal's Still/CCC Camp resource, but the exact surviving parcel and lawful public access remain unverified | Military & Cold War / New Deal forestry / Naval stores | **Tier 4** — NO SIGNAL | https://dlg.usg.edu/record/dlg_ggpd_i-ga-bf600-b-pp1-bf67-b3-s10 · https://dlg.usg.edu/record/dlg_ggpd_i-ga-bf600-b-pp1-bf67-b4-s10 · https://dlg.usg.edu/record/dlg_ggpd_i-ga-bf600-b-pp1-bf67-b4-s11 · https://dca.georgia.gov/document/plans/community-assessment-2007-6/download | NO-ANCHOR; do not infer a route from the five-mile historical description |
